title: Hyperspectral trait selection helps identify GhST7 in cotton salt tolerance
summary: Bowei Xu and colleagues at the Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences and collaborating institutions analyzed 419 upland cotton accessions using time-series hyperspectral traits, hierarchical filtering and GWAS. Random Forest, PLS-DA and LASSO consensus reduced 14,336 image-derived traits to 47 core traits used in the association analysis, which identified GhST7. The authors report functional support from gene-editing and overexpression experiments and associate promoter haplotypes with expression and salt-response differences. Work was performed in controlled seedling conditions; independent cotton populations and field-level breeding effects remain unestablished.
ai_technology: Random Forest, PLS-DA and LASSO consensus trait selection coupled to hyperspectral phenotyping and GWAS
organization: Institute of Cotton Research, Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences; Northwest Center of the National Technology Innovation Center for Saline-Alkali Agriculture; Henan Academy of Agricultural Sciences; Wuhan Greenpheno Science and Technology Co., Ltd.; Huazhong Agricultural University

evidence.tested: In 419 upland cotton accessions, machine-learning consensus retained 47 core traits from 14,336 hyperspectral i-traits for GWAS, which identified GhST7. The paper reports CRISPR knockout, VIGS, haplotype-specific overexpression and promoter assays supporting a role in salt response.
evidence.unknown: Validation is controlled and focused on seedlings. Independent populations and field-level breeding performance were not established.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning consensus feature selection reduces hyperspectral traits used as GWAS phenotypes; it supports prioritization of GhST7, while functional experiments test the candidate gene.

source_review.scope: Primary source full text reviewed for title, authorship, Methods, Results, version date and stated limitations.
